I stay in the hollow. The rain is loud, the wind is strong, and the world is dark. I sit still, I listen, and I wait. The storm is not a threat. It is just a part of the night. I do not move. I do not fly. I am safe in the oak. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I strike. It is a perfect evening. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I have enemies. The goshawk is always a threat. It hunts in the day and I hunt at night. I have seen it from the oak, waiting. It has sharp eyes and sharp talons. I do not like it.

Then there are the crows. They come near the meadow and scold me. They think they are clever, but they are not. I have watched them from the branch and waited for them to leave.

The road is dangerous. The lights are bright and the cars are fast. I have seen the lights from the oak and heard the cars. I do not like the road.

But I am not afraid. I have my hollow and my meadow. I have my calls and my silence. I am Hoot. I am the owl. I am the hunter.

I find food by sound. I listen for the rustle of small animals in the undergrowth, the scuttle of a mouse, the squeak of a shrew. My ears are wide and I can turn my head to listen in all directions. I was hunting. The meadow was quiet, but there were voles. I heard them under the leaves. I waited, then struck. The wind was cold, and the stars were bright. I called to my mate, and she answered.
